subject: Residency acceptance criteria & failover milestones - NexusBank private VPC
messages:
From: Amit Chawla <amit.chawla@nexusbank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@nexusbank.com
Date: Sat, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Residency questions and acceptance criteria for Private VPC pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and network teams are working through the residency checklist for a Private VPC pilot spanning our EU production tenancy and a warm-standby site in APAC. Before we get to procurement, can you confirm the acceptance criteria we should sign off on for the pilot? In particular: 

- Proof of data residency (data at rest and egress controls)
- Network isolation and peering topology (diagram)
- KMS/HSM integration options and key custody model
- Recovery and failover timeline for cross-region outages (RTO/RPO targets)
- Audit evidence (logs, access history) for a SOC2-type review

I've attached our initial questionnaire (nexusbank_residency_questions.xlsx) with a few extra items. Procurement is looped to keep things moving.

Could you share a compact set of acceptance criteria that maps to the above items so we can align legal and infra?

Best,
Amit
Amit Chawla
Head of Cloud Architecture, NexusBank
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
To: Amit Chawla <amit.chawla@nexusbank.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com, procurement@nexusbank.com
Date: Sat, 23 May 2027 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency questions and acceptance criteria for Private VPC pilot

Amit —

Thanks for the clear list. I've translated your questionnaire into a concise acceptance checklist for the pilot (high level + evidence). See summary below and I attached our topology diagram and a short KMS compatibility matrix.

Acceptance checklist (pilot scope):

1) Data residency evidence
   - All customer persistent volumes pinned to EU region A (logical tenancy mapping) for production traffic during the pilot window.
   - Evidence: snapshot of storage placement, S3-like object metadata export, and signed control-plane audit snapshot.

2) Network isolation & topology
   - Private VPC peering between NexusBank EU VPC and Redwood Private cluster; no public egress except through NexusBank-controlled NAT.
   - Evidence: BGP/peering configs, iptables/eBPF rules sample, and the attached topology PDF (redwood_private_vpc_topology_v1.pdf).

3) KMS/HSM options
   - Customer brings KMS keys via external key wrap or Redwood-managed wrapped keys; HSM-backed KMS supported in bring-your-own-key mode.
   - Evidence: key registration artifact and KMS integration test logs.

4) Failover & recovery
   - Canary failover test executed in dry-run mode with < 15m control-plane failover time; data RPO target: 1 minute for active caches, RTO target: 10 minutes for route switch to APAC standby.
   - Evidence: failover playbook runbook and run logs.

5) Audit & access evidence
   - Timestamped access logs retained for 90 days in EU region, immutable export available for compliance review.
   - Evidence: log export sample and signed attestation.

Next actions I propose:
- Redwood to return a single-page acceptance criteria doc that matches the above + attachments.
- Schedule a 45-min technical alignment call next week (network + security).
- Naomi (CC) will draft the minimal evidence bundle we can hand to your compliance reviewers.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_topology_v1.pdf, kms-hsm-compat-matrix.csv

I'll follow up with a short doc and a proposed meeting slot.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partnerships & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Amit Chawla <amit.chawla@nexusbank.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 24 May 2027 08:19:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency questions and acceptance criteria for Private VPC pilot

Amit/Vanessa — quick network note from infra: 

- Topology notes: We'll deploy a pair of control-plane instances in EU-A and a warm-standby control-plane in APAC-B. Data plane (GPU hosts) will be pinned to EU for pilot. Cross-region replication will use encrypted links over your private interconnect; no public IP NAT required.

- Peering specifics: We recommend using route-based VPN + BGP with MD5 auth for the peering session. For the failover window we'll add a route preference policy (local-preference) so EU remains preferred unless health checks fail.

- KMS integration: We support both external KMS calls (your HSM) and customer-managed keys in Redwood KMS via wrapped-key import. If you're using on-prem HSM, we'll publish a short integration playbook and run a key-signing test during onboarding.

I've attached a stub of the network runbook and a sample iptables export. We'll include a canary script to exercise control-plane failover without impacting the data-plane.

Attachments: redwood_network_runbook_stub.txt, iptables-sample.txt

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Amit Chawla <amit.chawla@nexusbank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@nexusbank.com, partners@edgecloud.io
Date: Mon, 25 May 2027 07:41:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency questions and acceptance criteria for Private VPC pilot

Vanessa / Karthik — this is helpful, thank you. A couple of clarifying asks from our side before we lock the pilot SOW: 

- Can Redwood commit to the 90-day log retention window in EU for the pilot and provide a sample signed export? Procurement will need that language in the SOW.
- For the KMS path: we prefer the bring-your-own-HSM option. Please confirm the exact API surface and a list of supported HSM vendors (HSM vendor list would be enough for procurement).
- Failover measurement: procurement will want a short definition of the measurement methodology for the <15m control-plane failover target. Can you include a test harness description and what counts as evidence?

Finally, partners@edgecloud.io is our cloud integration partner — they'll help with peering on their side. Procurement is asking for a single combined evidence bundle to attach to the SOW.

Can Naomi and Vanessa provide that bundle and the SOW wording by Wednesday EOD?

Best,
Amit

To: Amit Chawla <amit.chawla@nexusbank.com>, procurement@nexusbank.com

Subject: Re: Residency questions and acceptance criteria for Private VPC pilot

Amit — we can deliver the evidence bundle and SOW snippets by Wednesday EOD. Commitments we will include in the pilot SOW: 

- Log retention: 90 days immutable export (EU region) — sample signed export attached to evidence bundle.
- HSM vendors supported: Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and Entrust (detailed compat matrix attached). We'll map your vendor to the integration playbook during onboarding.
- Failover measurement: We'll include the test harness and criteria: 
   * Measurement methodology: controlled canary that drains one control-plane instance, triggers route-health checks, and promotes standby. Timer starts at failure detection and ends when route convergence + control-plane heartbeats indicate active.
   * Evidence: annotated logs from the canary run, BGP convergence timestamps, control-plane heartbeat timestamps, and an operator-signed run report.

Action items:
- Naomi will assemble the evidence bundle (signed log export, topology PDF, KMS compat CSV, example run report).
- I'll circulate a 1-page SOW snippet for procurement to attach to your contract.
- Schedule: Proposed technical alignment call Thursday 10:00 UTC — please confirm.

Thanks everyone — we'll attach the bundle to the Drive link and drop the HubSpot deal note.

Attachments to follow: nexusbank_residency_evidence_bundle.zip (will upload to Drive)

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
